title: Topological Recursion and Quantum Path Signatures
authors: Inês Aniceto, Thomas Cass, Samuel Crew
abstract: We introduce a non-commutative Laplace transform between functionals on path space and formal series in a tensor algebra, under which a natural convolution of path functionals becomes an algebraic product of series. Applying it to a random unitary matrix-valued path development - the quantum path signature - we show that the governing planar loop equations take a non-commutative spectral form. We then extend the loop equations to a $1/N$ genus expansion, organised by topological recursion, and obtain a hierarchy of integral equations on path space for the corrections.
summary: This work develops a sophisticated mathematical machinery using a non-commutative Laplace transform to relate path space observables (quantum path signatures) to algebraic equations from random matrix theory. It successfully derives the full genus expansion of these loop equations, providing deep structural insights into quantum field theories governed by such spectral relations.
main_problem: The paper establishes a rigorous mathematical framework connecting path space analysis (quantum path signatures) to algebraic structures derived from random matrix theory via a non-commutative Laplace transform.
main_result: They successfully derive the genus-$g$ loop equations for the quantum path signature, confirming consistency across multiple computational methods up to genus one and providing a systematic expansion in $1/N$.
method: The core method involves introducing and utilizing a non-commutative Laplace transform that maps convolution products on path space functionals (signatures) to algebraic products of formal power series.
model_or_system: The analysis centers on the quantum path signature, derived from random unitary matrix-valued paths $U(\gamma)$, which is related to Wilson loops in gauge theory and planar limits of matrix models.
key_observables: Quantum Path Signature ($S$), Planar Wilson Line Observable ($W$), Genus-$g$ corrections ($W_g$), and the non-commutative resolvent ($R_\mu$).
important_parameters: The large-$N$ limit (planar limit), genus $g$, and path geometry $\gamma(t)$ are key parameters.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes factorial decay of the signature moments for the existence of the planar limit, and it notes that the full solution theory for interacting models remains open due to non-closure.
figures_summary: Not specified in detail, but the structure implies showing recursive relations (e.g., Eq. 66) and comparing results from different computational approaches (discretized loops vs. combinatorial forms).
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first defining the non-commutative Laplace transform to map path convolution to algebraic products; it then applies this to derive the planar loop equation; subsequently, it extends this framework to systematically calculate genus-$g$ corrections ($W_g$) via integral equations.
why_interesting: While highly abstract, the techniques developed—relating geometric/path integrals (signatures) to formal power series and spectral curves—are powerful tools for analyzing quantum field theories in dimensions where standard methods fail.
